_comment: Source of truth for the upstream CLI versions this repo has explicitly accepted as supported. The upstream-watch workflow compares npm's `latest` dist-tag against `accepted`; a human bumps `accepted` only after a compatibility review. Never edited by automation. See support/README.md.

opencode.label: OpenCode
notes: Added at the app level (remote-v2 rebuild, Refs #996): both OpenCode runtimes wrap this one CLI, and the app-level watch previously had no entry — the packages carry their own files (packages/opencode-terminal-headless and packages/opencode-headless), but nothing compared the npm latest against an APP-accepted version. Acceptance rides the terminal package's review (1.18.30, live-recorded); the structured runtime's SSE vocabulary is stringly-parsed with an unknown_event catch-all, so the same compatibility-pass discipline applies per package before this number moves.

1.18.31 — accepted as the bundled-runtime pin (Refs #994). Basis: the official release asset verified by archive+binary sha256, the full deterministic suites green (terminal package, app setup/provider-switch, typecheck), and production evidence — the app has been driving 1.18.31 TUI panes, conditions included, in daily use since 2026-09-14. The recorded live compatibility pass could NOT discriminate 1.18.31 from 1.18.30 on 2026-09-19: it times out waiting for the permission condition identically on both versions, including the same 1.18.30 the Stage 0 recordings passed against, so that failure is environmental rather than a pin regression (tracked in #1009). npm latest is 1.18.31, so this acceptance also clears the upstream-watch drift. Re-run #1009's scenario once fixed before treating the live suite as acceptance evidence again.

pi.label: Pi
notes: Added with the Pi terminal provider (Refs #1132). Acceptance rides packages/pi-terminal-headless's own support/upstream-versions.json and its Stage 0 recordings (research/census-2026-09-22.md, recorded on 0.87.1); the app pins the same number. Pi ships breaking changes in 0.x minors, so a bump needs that package's compatibility pass (re-record with its probe, diff the corpus) before this number moves.
